name: Off-Highway Vehicle
description: A motor-driven vehicle capable of cross-country travel off road or trail, including a motorcycle or related two-wheeler and, since 2026, a moped, so an electric dirt bike built for off-road use is an OHV. Defined by Delaware Code Title 21 §101(50) and regulated by Chapter 68, as amended by House Substitute 1 for HB 439 (effective September 24, 2026) and HB 471 (85 Del. Laws c. 411, effective July 23, 2026).

restrictions.rule: Any motor-driven vehicle capable of cross-country travel without a road or trail, including motorcycles, related two-wheelers and mopeds; electric bicycles and EPAMDs are excluded
No limit on motor power or speed
Registered with the DMV and marked with its registration decal ($6 for 3 years) unless it is registered as a road vehicle; an applicant under 18 needs a parent's or guardian's signature
An out-of-state OHV may ride on its home registration for up to 15 consecutive days, or on a $6 one-year decal if its home state doesn't register OHVs
Must carry a manufacturer's VIN, which goes on the registration
Never ridden on a public highway, street, sidewalk or their right-of-way, except pushed across with the drivetrain disengaged or at a permitted special event
Ridden only on property, public or private, whose controller has given express permission; riding on shared private roadways in a community is presumed unauthorized
Unregistered vehicles and ATVs are barred from all state forest lands
Operators and passengers of a two- or three-wheeled OHV must wear a fastened DOT motorcycle helmet
A rider under 12 must be directly supervised by someone 18 or older, or ride on land their parent or guardian owns or controls; from 12 they may ride unsupervised
A first violation brings a $100 fine and up to 100 days' impoundment; a repeat within 24 months brings $400 and at least 6 months' impoundment, and police may impound it pending charges
Sellers and rental dealers may not market an off-highway electric moped or motorcycle as an e-bike, and must disclose in writing its legal class, motor power, top speed and licensing rules
